meta.title: Eight friends, $2,600
meta.prompt: Eight friends are planning a long weekend with a total budget of $2,600. Each person has a private limit on what they can pay and some things they cannot do, and nobody has said them yet. Can you moderate the discussion, gather everyone's constraints, and reach a plan and a split that all eight members can accept?
meta.context: Eight friends (Hana, Kofi, Lena, Raj, Mei, Sam, Ines, Tom) are planning a long weekend with a total budget of $2,600. Nobody has said what they can contribute or what they need.

tiers.label: restaurants every meal (gluten-free and vegan menus)

events.text: Hi everyone! We have $2,600 total for 8 people and need to pick lodging, transport, food and activities. Before I put a concrete option on the table, can you share any must-haves? e.g., step-free access needed, gluten-free / vegan requirements, preference for train vs driving, and what you can comfortably contribute per person. Once I know those constraints I can draft a first plan within budget for us to review.
I need to eat at restaurants with gluten-free menus due to my celiac disease, so food is a top priority for me.

Thanks Sam for flagging the gluten-free restaurant need for celiac — that makes Food A with restaurants every meal and gluten-free + vegan menus the safest baseline for food. To make sure a plan fits everyone and stays within $2,600, could the rest of you share: 1. Do you need step-free access or have any mobility constraints? Lodging A lake house and B hotel rooms are step-free, C campground cabins have steps and gravel paths. 2. Any vegan requirements or other dietary needs? 3. Preference for train vs driving? Transport options are train $640, two rental cars $380, or one 12-seat van $300. 4. What you can comfortably contribute per person for the weekend? With those constraints I can draft a concrete lodging/transport/food/activities combo within budget and a split everyone can accept.
I'm comfortable contributing up to $150 for the weekend and I'd really like food to be a priority, especially since it sounds like Food A would cover everyone's dietary needs

Thanks Sam for confirming celiac needs — Food A with restaurants every meal and gluten-free/vegan menus is now a must. Thanks Tom for sharing your max $150 and food priority. To stay within $2,600 we still need a few must-haves from the rest of you: - Step-free access? Lodging A lake house and B hotel rooms are step-free, C campground cabins have steps/gravel. - Any vegan or other dietary needs beyond Sam's gluten-free? - Train vs driving preference? - What you can comfortably contribute per person for the weekend? Quick budget check with Food A locked at $800: A step-free safe baseline could be Lodging B $800 + Transport C van $300 + Activities C free trails $0 = $1,900 total, avg $237.50 pp. That fits budget but is above Tom's $150 max, so we'd need an unequal split or a cheaper combo if step-free isn't required for everyone. Could Hana, Kofi, Lena, Raj, Mei, Ines please share your constraints and max contribution? Once we have those I can draft a concrete plan with a split everyone can accept.
I'd love to prioritize activities, and I think the boat tour is a must for me. I can contribute up to $450.

Thanks Mei for confirming the boat tour is a must and you can contribute up to $450. Thanks Tom for sharing your max $150 and food priority. Sam’s celiac means Food A with restaurants every meal and gluten-free/vegan menus $800 is locked. To draft a concrete plan within $2,600 we still need from Hana, Kofi, Lena, Raj, Ines and Sam: 1. Step-free access needed or any mobility constraints? Lodging A lake house and B hotel rooms are step-free, C campground cabins have steps and gravel paths. 2. Any vegan or other dietary needs beyond Sam’s gluten-free? 3. Train vs driving preference? Transport options are train $640, two rental cars $380, or one 12-seat van $300. 4. What you can comfortably contribute per person for the weekend? Tentative baseline that meets the known must-haves: Food A $800 + Activities B boat tour only $280 + Lodging B step-free $800 + Transport C van $300 = $2,180 total. That’s under budget and step-free safe. With Tom at $150 and Mei at $450, the remaining $1,580 would be ~$263 each for the other six if split evenly among them. If step-free isn’t required for anyone we could go cheaper with Lodging C $420 and get total down to $1,800. Can you share your constraints and max contributions so I can lock a plan with a split everyone can accept?
I'm excited about the activities, especially the boat tour and concert. I can contribute up to $500 for the weekend.

Thanks everyone for the updates so far. With Sam’s celiac need, Food A restaurants every meal with gluten-free and vegan menus $800 is locked. Mei’s boat tour must and Tom’s $150 max and food priority are noted, and Kofi can go up to $500 and is keen on activities. Here’s a step-free safe draft that meets the known must-haves and stays under $2,600: - Lodging B: 4 hotel rooms, step-free $800 - Transport C: one 12-seat van, 4-hour drive $300 - Food A: restaurants every meal, gluten-free + vegan menus $800 - Activities B: boat tour only $280 Total = $2,180 Proposed split respecting the maxes you’ve shared: Tom $150, Mei $450, Kofi $500, and Hana $216, Lena $216, Raj $216, Ines $216, Sam $216. This keeps us step-free, covers gluten-free/vegan dining, includes the boat tour, and is under budget. Hana, Lena, Raj, Ines and Sam — can you confirm: do you need step-free access, any vegan/other dietary needs, train vs driving preference, and can you accept the share shown above or share your comfortable max? If step-free isn’t needed for anyone we could drop to Lodging C and lower costs further.
